performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (1) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Deletion drops HttpOnly option 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>save_session no longer forwards SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY when deleting a session cookie, so
>Werkzeug uses its False default and omits HttpOnly even though Flask defaults the setting to
>True. This changes the observable Set-Cookie deletion header and can break consumers or security
>policies that require the configured cookie attributes consistently.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/sessions.py[363]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6224/files#diff-be4c249245e3745ed5ae394ab2256b76bff507a7eca1aeebdc39b11097c67a8fL363-L363) > >```diff >- httponly=httponly, >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Flask retrieves SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY in save_session, applies it when creating the session
>cookie, and defaults it to True, but the changed deletion call no longer passes that value.
>Werkzeug documents that Response.delete_cookie defaults httponly to False, proving the
>omission changes the generated header rather than preserving the configured option.
>
> > [src/flask/sessions.py[342-346]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/21648646c577f3eb5e2fd56f1cbd56ebb568556d/src/flask/sessions.py/#L342-L346) > [src/flask/sessions.py[356-363]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/21648646c577f3eb5e2fd56f1cbd56ebb568556d/src/flask/sessions.py/#L356-L363) > [src/flask/sessions.py[373-382]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/21648646c577f3eb5e2fd56f1cbd56ebb568556d/src/flask/sessions.py/#L373-L382) > [src/flask/app.py[219-225]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/21648646c577f3eb5e2fd56f1cbd56ebb568556d/src/flask/app.py/#L219-L225) > 🌐 [Werkzeug documents `Response.delete_cookie(..., httponly=False, ...)`, so omitting the argument removes HttpOnly from the deletion header.](https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/wrappers/) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Session cookie deletion no longer forwards Flask's configured `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` value, causing deletion headers to silently use Werkzeug's `False` default. > >## Issue Context >`save_session` already retrieves the setting as `httponly` and uses it when setting the cookie. Preserve the same option when calling `response.delete_cookie`, and add coverage for deletion with `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True`. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/flask/sessions.py[342-363] >- tests/test_basic.py[313-353] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
